A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Directed Graph|directed graph]] with edge weights $w$, no negative cycles, and vertices $s$, $t$ with $t$ reachable from $s$.
Then:
:$\map \delta {s, t} = \max \set {\map \pi t - \map \pi s: \map \pi v - \map \pi u \le \map w {u, v} \text { for every edge } \tuple {u, v} }$

B_source.statement: If a [[Definition:Linear Program|linear program]] $\min \set {\mathbf c^\intercal \mathbf x: \mathbf A \mathbf x = \mathbf b, \mathbf x \ge \mathbf 0}$ and its dual $\max \set {\mathbf b^\intercal \mathbf y: \mathbf A^\intercal \mathbf y \le \mathbf c}$ are both feasible, then their optimal values are equal.

substitutions.primal variables: flow on edges sending one unit from s to t

object_map.reformulation: Write shortest path as a min-cost unit flow; its dual assigns potentials to vertices, constrained by the edge weights.

validity_conditions: The incidence matrix is totally unimodular, so the primal optimum is attained by a path.
No negative cycles is what makes the distance function itself a feasible potential.
proof_plan:
The primal program minimizes $\sum_e \map w e x_e$ subject to flow conservation sending one unit from $s$ to $t$, with $\mathbf x \ge \mathbf 0$.
Its constraint matrix is the vertex-edge incidence matrix.
The dual has one variable $\map \pi v$ per vertex and maximizes $\map \pi t - \map \pi s$ subject to $\map \pi v - \map \pi u \le \map w {u, v}$.

The primal is feasible as $t$ is reachable, and $\pi = \map \delta {s, \cdot}$ is dual feasible by the triangle inequality, as there are no negative cycles.
By the source result, the optima agree.
